# daemon

the datashell daemon in the browser, like basims daemon on the cli. the vault runs in a worker (`lib/vault-worker.js`) that owns the storage, so all tabs share one vault, and every tab gets a stand in for it that works like the vault itself.

```js
// page (lib/datashell.js)
const daemon = require('daemon')
const vault = await daemon.up({ input, local: { session_get_username: () => localStorage.getItem('username') } })
const user = await vault.user
await vault.vault_put('key', 'value')
for await (const change of vault.get_vault_bee().watch()) {}

// worker (lib/vault-worker.js)
daemon.serve(port, vault)
```

- `daemon.up({ url, input, local, on_wait })` starts the worker or connects to it. a SharedWorker (`url`, default `vault.bundle.js`) that all tabs share, or a dedicated worker where there is none, then only one tab runs it at a time and `on_wait` runs while another tab has it. it also does the webrtc for the worker (webrtc-bridge) and gives the stand in. functions in `local` run in the page itself (the session values live in the pages localStorage)
- `daemon.connect(port, local)` is the same stand in for a port u wired up yourself (test/web.js does that)
- `daemon.serve(port, object)` answers the calls of one page

## how it works

- reading properties on the stand in only builds a path, the call, `await` or `for await` at the end sends it as one `call` message `{ ref, path, args }`, the worker runs it and replies. messages are our `{ head, refs, type, data, meta }` format (`make_tx` from iframe-runtime), a reply points to its call with `refs.cause`
- plain data (numbers, strings, arrays, plain objects, Map, Set, typed arrays) is copied to the page. anything else (the vault bee, a watcher, the user vault) stays in the worker under a `ref` number and the page gets a new stand in for it, with its simple properties copied (`user.username`)
- a function the page passes in (`on_seed_phrase`, `on_paired`) stays in the page. the worker gets a function that sends a `callback` message and waits for the pages answer
- the worker can also tell the pages to write their localStorage (`storage`), show an `alert`, or `reload`, things a worker cant do itself
